paragraphs: Virtual screening searches large chemical libraries for compounds that score well while satisfying practical constraints. Libraries containing tens of billions of candidates make direct scoring expensive: a routine campaign may examine fewer than 0.1% of them. Changing requirements can also make previous search work difficult to reuse.

APEX addresses this problem with a neural surrogate that predicts objectives and constraints using the library’s combinatorial structure. Its inexpensive predictions make exhaustive enumeration possible on a consumer GPU in under a minute. The distinction is important: retrieval is exact according to the approximate predictions, rather than guaranteed exact according to the original scoring function.

The authors also construct a benchmark containing more than 10 million compounds, with docking scores for five targets and computed physicochemical properties. These annotations allow retrieved candidates to be checked against the true best candidates under benchmark objectives and constraints. APEX shows consistently strong retrieval accuracy and runtime against alternative methods, supporting exhaustive surrogate search as a practical screening strategy.
icml-2026-apex-approximate-but-exhaustiv.tldr: APEX searches entire combinatorial chemical libraries using fast neural predictions, enabling exact retrieval under approximate scores.

paragraphs: An assistive language model may need to understand someone who cannot reliably enter clean text or repair an unclear request. Ordinary accuracy and noise-robustness tests do not fully capture this situation. A useful response must recover the intended request while avoiding invented interpretations and unnecessary cognitive demands.

Assistive Prompt Mediation evaluates that combination directly. It treats assistance as recovering intent from accessibility-impaired input without asking for clarification, and separates intent preservation, cognitive burden, and hallucination risk. The evaluation covers eight languages, four accessibility-related noise classes, and ten frontier models. Varying impairment severity reveals how assistance changes as input becomes harder to interpret.

The results show that strong intent preservation can accompany greater burden or hallucinated mediation. Hallucination rates differ by more than twofold across noise types. The measured decision entropy also indicates systematic response patterns rather than unstable behavior. Together, these findings explain why conventional robustness scores can overestimate assistive reliability: success on the apparent task does not establish that the model handled the user’s accessibility constraints well.
icml-2026-assistive-prompt-mediation-eva.tldr: Assistive Prompt Mediation reveals trade-offs between recovering user intent, cognitive burden, and hallucination under accessibility constraints.

paragraphs: Generating rare examples requires deciding what counts as rare. Existing minority-sampling methods often use the generator’s own learned distribution, so unusual outputs reflect that model’s particular expectations. The paper instead seeks examples that are rare in a broader semantic sense, motivated by uses such as anomaly detection and creative generation.

The proposed method guides diffusion sampling with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, or JEPA. This world-model representation supplies an implicit density that identifies less common regions in its semantic space. Guidance moves generation toward those regions, making the JEPA’s representation the reference for rarity. The authors also develop computational approximations with theoretical error bounds to reduce the cost of applying this guidance.

Experiments cover unconditional generation, class-conditioned generation, and text-to-image generation. Across these settings, the authors report consistently better fidelity and semantic validity than generator-centered alternatives. The findings support using a separate, semantically rich representation to guide minority sampling, rather than relying entirely on the generator’s internal estimate of what is unusual.
icml-2026-beyond-generative-priors-minor.tldr: JEPA guidance steers diffusion toward semantically rare examples using a world-model representation as the reference for rarity.

paragraphs: Different input modalities do not always describe the same evidence. An image and a medical history, for example, can contribute distinct information to a classification decision. The paper studies this complementary setting, where explainable methods based on one shared similarity measure can struggle with evidence that differs across modalities and classes.

CAMP aligns evidence separately for each class using optimal transport. It also imposes geometric constraints intended to prevent one modality from dominating and to prevent representations from collapsing. These mechanisms organize multimodal prototypes into coherent reasoning patterns. The authors provide theoretical guarantees that the mechanisms eliminate these degeneracies without reducing the framework’s expressive capacity.

Across 16 public datasets, CAMP matches or exceeds large AutoML baselines while using fewer than one million trainable parameters; those baselines have more than 100 million parameters. End-to-end fine-tuning achieves state-of-the-art performance in the reported evaluation. The results suggest that explicitly organizing complementary evidence can support both competitive classification and an explainable prototype-based design.
icml-2026-camp-coherent-alignment-of-mul.tldr: CAMP aligns class-specific evidence across complementary modalities to combine interpretable prototypes with strong classification performance.

paragraphs: Causal discovery methods seek causal graph structure from data, but computation and memory become major obstacles as graphs grow. CauScale addresses both bottlenecks with a neural architecture that supports inference on graphs containing up to 1,000 nodes. Its design aims to retain useful structural evidence while reducing the resources needed to process it.

A reduction unit compresses data embeddings to improve time efficiency. Tied attention weights reduce memory requirements by avoiding separate attention maps for different axes. Two interacting streams preserve complementary information: one extracts relationships from observations, while the other incorporates statistical graph priors and maintains structural signals.

The method trains on 500-node graphs, a scale where the compared prior work encounters memory limits. Across tests varying graph size and causal mechanisms, the authors report 99.6% mean average precision in distribution and 84.4% out of distribution, with inference speedups ranging from fourfold to 13,000-fold over prior methods. These results show substantial scaling gains alongside strong reported discovery accuracy.
icml-2026-causcale-neural-causal-discove.tldr: CauScale combines compressed data representations and shared attention with two-stream reasoning to scale causal discovery to 1,000-node inference.

paragraphs: Constrained generation must produce valid outputs without unnecessarily narrowing their variety. Greedy constraint enforcement can change a language model’s distribution, while ordinary rejection sampling preserves the desired conditional distribution but repeatedly spends computation on invalid candidates. This tension matters in applications such as program fuzzing and molecular generation.

Constrained Adaptive Rejection Sampling starts with ordinary model sampling and remembers continuations that violate constraints. It stores them in a trie, a structure organized by shared prefixes, and removes their probability mass from later draws. Prefixes established as invalid are therefore never revisited. The method guarantees monotonically improving acceptance rates while retaining the exact distribution conditioned on validity.

Experiments show better efficiency, measured as model forward passes per valid sample, across several domains. CARS also produces greater sample diversity than greedy constrained decoding and methods that only approximate the model’s distribution. Its central contribution is to reuse information from failed draws: rejecting an output improves future sampling instead of simply discarding the computation.
icml-2026-constrained-adaptive-rejection.tldr: CARS remembers invalid continuations to make rejection sampling more efficient while preserving the exact constrained output distribution.

paragraphs: A time-series classifier trained on one source domain must generalize without examples of the other domains it will encounter. Synthetic training data can help expand its experience, but generated examples may lack variety or introduce noise. CURE addresses this problem by controlling both the semantic content and other variation in generated sequences.

The method first separates source representations into semantic-aware and semantic-free components. It retrieves trajectories with similar semantics to build the semantic-aware context, while adversarial learning develops semantic-free contexts. Both types jointly condition a diffusion model, providing guidance for producing varied examples that retain useful semantic information.

CURE also changes its expansion process during training. A memory bank progressively updates the semantic-free contexts, and measurements of boundary properties guide dynamic filtering of generated data. These components aim to make expansion adaptable and optimization stable. Benchmark experiments validate the method’s effectiveness. The contribution is a coordinated approach to data augmentation in which representation separation, conditional generation, and sample filtering work together under the single-source-domain constraint.
icml-2026-cure-context-driven-diffusion-.tldr: CURE combines semantic and semantic-free diffusion guidance with progressive filtering to improve time-series classification beyond one training domain.

paragraphs: How can a network learn hierarchical language structure from sentences without being explicitly shown their parses? This paper investigates which statistical patterns make that learning possible and how they affect the amount of training data required. It uses probabilistic context-free grammars as a controlled setting for studying these questions.

The authors introduce a tunable grammar family in which ambiguity and correlations across structural scales can be varied. They then construct an inference algorithm inspired by deep convolutional networks. This provides a proposed learning mechanism that connects particular language statistics to learnability and sample complexity, rather than only describing representations after training.

The central idea is that correlations at different scales can resolve ambiguities that remain unclear locally. As those ambiguities are lifted, hierarchical representations can emerge. Experiments with both convolutional and transformer architectures support the theoretical predictions. The resulting framework explains how local statistical evidence and broader correlations can work together to support parsing in the controlled language family studied.
icml-2026-deep-networks-learn-to-parse-u.tldr: A controlled grammar framework links correlations across scales to how neural networks learn hierarchical parsing and how much data they need.

paragraphs: Removing memorized information from a language model creates a subtle usability requirement. The model should forget the targeted knowledge, yet users may still want it to work with that information when they explicitly provide it in a prompt. The paper calls this latter ability contextual utility.

Standard unlearning evaluations measure forgetting and preservation of performance on information that should remain. The authors add the contextual-use dimension and systematically evaluate six state-of-the-art methods. They find that these methods consistently damage the ability to use forgotten material when it is supplied again, exposing a cost that the usual evaluation misses.

To address that problem, the authors add a plug-in term to unlearning objectives that explicitly preserves contextual utility. Experiments show recovery to near the original level of contextual performance while maintaining effective forgetting and retain-set utility. The findings distinguish access to memorized knowledge from the ability to process supplied information, and show that unlearning objectives can account for both.
icml-2026-forget-to-know-remember-to-use.tldr: An added unlearning objective preserves a model’s ability to use explicitly supplied information while still forgetting its memorized version.

paragraphs: Body motion combines spatial structure with changes over time. Phase manifolds represent local periodic patterns in a compact latent space, but existing approaches are often tied to particular skeletons and limited motion distributions. FunPhase develops a more flexible representation for both predicting motion and generating new motion.

Its periodic autoencoder reconstructs movement through a function-space formulation instead of decoding only at discrete time steps. This produces smooth trajectories that can be sampled at arbitrary temporal resolutions. The same interpretable phase manifold supports prediction and latent-diffusion generation, allowing these tasks to share a common representation.

The model generalizes across skeletons and datasets and supports motion super-resolution and partial-body completion. Against prior periodic autoencoders, the authors report substantially lower reconstruction error and improvements of at least 45% across all evaluated metrics. Motion generation performs on par with state-of-the-art methods. These findings connect improved reconstruction with a broader range of uses, particularly where motion must be represented across different bodies or temporal sampling rates.
icml-2026-funphase-a-periodic-functional.tldr: FunPhase learns a continuous phase-based motion representation that supports flexible temporal sampling, prediction, and generation across skeletons.

paragraphs: Neural operators learn mappings between functions while retaining independence from a particular discretization. Standard deterministic versions produce one prediction, leaving uncertainty unmodeled. Diffusion last layer, or DLL, adds a modular probabilistic output head so an operator backbone can represent a distribution of possible target fields.

DLL expresses each target field through a compact, input-dependent expansion inspired by the Karhunen–Loève expansion. A conditional diffusion model learns the distribution of the expansion’s coefficients. Modeling uncertainty in this smaller coefficient space makes distributional prediction efficient while preserving the structural advantages of the underlying operator.

On stochastic partial differential equation benchmarks with random forcing, DLL captures output distributions well and competes with pixel-space and conventional latent diffusion approaches. In deterministic tasks involving long autoregressive rollouts, it improves stability over the backbone and provides useful uncertainty estimates as prediction errors accumulate. These results suggest that a learned coefficient space can serve as a practical interface between operator learning and probabilistic diffusion modeling.
icml-2026-generative-neural-operators-th.tldr: DLL adds diffusion over compact field coefficients to neural operators, enabling uncertainty estimates and improving reported rollout stability.

paragraphs: Cooperating embodied agents often see only part of their environment. When each uses a language model to plan locally, their choices can conflict. Explicit messages can help coordinate them, but communication may be expensive or unavailable. This paper studies how agents can cooperate without taking explicit messaging actions.

Contextual Tacit Communication uses a joint language-model value score to align decentralized choices. Its gradient-free procedure measures context-dependent value corrections through residual banding, identifying actions associated with miscoordination. It then stores the resulting coordination signals in a retrieval-augmented Tacit Rule Memory.

At execution time, retrieved rules enter the agents’ prompts and guide cooperation. This reuses coordination knowledge without requiring online message exchange for each decision. Experiments on VIKI, C-WAH, and TDW-MAT show improved cooperation over the evaluated baselines and lower runtime overhead than communication-based methods. The findings support converting joint coordination assessments into reusable contextual rules that individual agents can consult when acting under partial observability.
icml-2026-great-minds-think-alike-contex.tldr: Contextual Tacit Communication turns joint coordination signals into retrieved prompt rules for cooperation without explicit message actions.

paragraphs: Transformer-based neural operators can handle irregular physical domains, but standard attention gives every token pair the same interaction budget. This overlooks the fact that distant physical interactions can often be compressed. Classical fast solvers exploit that structure by organizing nearby and faraway interactions hierarchically.

The Hyperbolic Neural Operator brings a related hierarchy into learnable attention. Hyperbolic geometry naturally accommodates the exponential branching of trees, whereas representing such hierarchies in Euclidean space introduces distortion. HNO constructs a continuous Gibbs kernel using stabilized geodesic distances on the Lorentz hyperboloid, making the geometry part of how interactions are weighted.

This design encourages routing across multiple scales in a manner analogous to the Fast Multipole Method, while keeping a unified attention mechanism. Across six partial differential equation benchmarks and two large unstructured computational fluid dynamics tasks, HNO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in the reported evaluation. Mean relative error falls by up to 40% against leading baselines, supporting the value of geometry that reflects hierarchical physical interactions.
icml-2026-hyperbolic-neural-operator-ff6.tldr: HNO uses hyperbolic geometry to organize attention across physical scales, improving reported neural-operator accuracy on PDE and fluid-dynamics tasks.

paragraphs: Insertion-based masked diffusion generates sequences by adding positions and revealing their token contents. Existing methods use fixed schedules for these operations, regardless of the data. For structured objects such as molecules, choosing an order that reflects the developing sequence can reduce uncertainty about which action to take next.

LoFlexMDM learns data-dependent insertion and unmasking rates. To make this possible, the authors extend discrete flow matching to variable-length sequences and introduce a tractable schedule parameterization. A joint objective trains both the generator and its target order dynamics, so the sequence-building process itself becomes part of what the model learns.

On de novo molecule generation, sample quality improves over FlexMDM by up to 17.5%; on generation constrained by molecular fragments, the improvement reaches 6.7%. These are reported gains for the evaluated tasks, demonstrating that learned generation orders can help in both settings. The contribution combines that flexibility with tractable training, allowing the model to adapt when it inserts and resolves tokens.
icml-2026-insertion-based-sequence-gener.tldr: LoFlexMDM learns when to insert and unmask tokens, improving reported molecular generation quality while retaining tractable training.

paragraphs: Generating reasoning from a question and an already supplied answer can produce an explanation shaped by that answer. The paper studies this anchoring through three measurement levels: surface wording, entropy dynamics, and probabilistic dependence on the answer. This separates visible copying from deeper dependence in the generated reasoning.

Instructing a model to ignore the answer reduces lexical overlap but increases the other two forms of anchoring. The authors attribute this to active monitoring of the forbidden answer. Their alternative, Structural Skeleton-guided Reasoning, first generates an answer-invariant functional outline, then uses that content-neutral structure to guide the full reasoning trace.

Experiments on open-ended reasoning benchmarks show that this structural approach consistently mitigates anchoring. A distilled version learns skeleton-guided reasoning from teacher-generated traces and achieves improvements of up to 10% over suppression baselines while reducing out-of-distribution degradation. The findings show why an explanation that looks less similar to the answer may still depend on it more strongly, motivating measurements beyond wording.
icml-2026-measuring-and-mitigating-post-.tldr: Answer-invariant reasoning skeletons reduce post-hoc anchoring more effectively than instructing models to ignore a supplied answer.

paragraphs: Quantum error correction protects logical information by distributing it across redundant physical qubits. A decoder interprets detected error signals and chooses a correction. Minimum Weight Perfect Matching is a common graph-based decoder whose edge weights determine which error chains it considers most likely.

Neural Minimum Weight Perfect Matching learns dynamic edge weights while retaining the classical matching algorithm. A graph neural network extracts local features from the error syndrome, and a Transformer captures longer-range dependencies. Their predictions adapt the weights used by matching. Because the matching operation is not differentiable, the authors introduce a proxy loss that enables end-to-end training.

For the toric code under depolarizing noise, the paper reports thresholds of 17.9% and 10.95%, approaching the cited maximum-likelihood bounds of 18.9% and 11.0%. These findings support the hybrid design: neural components interpret local and global evidence, while a structured matching algorithm uses that information to decode errors. The reported results are specific to the code and noise setting studied.
icml-2026-neural-minimum-weight-perfect-.tldr: NMWPM learns context-dependent graph weights for classical quantum-error matching, reaching reported thresholds near maximum-likelihood bounds.

paragraphs: Diffusion and flow models can represent robot control policies, but improving an entire generative policy requires learning through its multistep generation process. OGPO combines off-policy critics, which reuse collected experience, with a modified PPO objective that propagates policy gradients through the full process using critic evaluations as terminal rewards.

The method also introduces success-buffer regularization and two-sided conservative advantages to limit over-exploitation of critic estimates. These stabilization techniques apply to both state-based and pixel-based settings. Alongside the algorithm, the paper investigates mechanisms and failure modes involved in full-policy improvement from off-policy data.

OGPO achieves reported state-of-the-art performance across multitask manipulation, precise insertion, and dexterous control. It substantially outperforms compared approaches based on policy steering or residual corrections. The authors also report bringing poorly initialized behavior-cloning policies close to full task success without expert data in the online replay buffer and with little task-specific tuning. They qualify the uniqueness of that capability as being to their knowledge.
icml-2026-ogpo-sample-efficient-full-fin.tldr: OGPO reuses experience and trains through full generative policies to improve robot control, with stabilization against critic over-exploitation.

paragraphs: Extra information available during training can help a language-model agent solve difficult, long tasks. The challenge is transferring that capability to an agent that must act without the extra information later. This becomes especially difficult when a frontier model exposes successful action sequences but keeps its internal reasoning private.

The proposed π-Distill framework jointly trains a teacher conditioned on privileged information and a student that does not receive it. Both operate within one shared-parameter model. This arrangement lets the teacher learn how to use the additional information while mitigating the distribution shift involved in transferring its behavior to the student.

Across multiple agent benchmarks, models, and forms of privileged information, π-Distill effectively transfers capabilities using action-only information. It matches or exceeds industry-standard pipelines that assume access to complete chain-of-thought supervision. The results show that observed actions can provide effective training guidance within this joint framework, even when the source agent’s reasoning is unavailable. Further analysis examines factors that enable successful learning with privileged information.
icml-2026-privileged-information-distill.tldr: π-Distill jointly trains a privileged teacher and unconditioned student to transfer agent capabilities from action-only supervision.

paragraphs: Representing nested symbolic structures creates a memory trade-off. Tensor Product Representations preserve structure but grow exponentially with recursive depth. Vector Symbolic Architectures keep a fixed dimensionality, but compression through superposition introduces noise that reduces capacity and fidelity. This paper proposes a different geometric way to organize recursive bindings.

Orthogonal Subspace Carving binds fillers to roles by projecting onto the null space of the role basis before combining them into a fixed-order tensor. These projections enforce orthogonality between bound structures within a static memory trace. The construction separates tensor order from structural depth, allowing deeper recursive binding without increasing the memory footprint.

The authors also show that component vectors can be orders of magnitude smaller than the memory tensor, yielding strong memory efficiency when many structures are superposed. A further mathematical contribution expresses Tensor Product Representations as a special case of binding in Clifford algebra and formulates OSC in that language. The work connects compact recursive memory to explicit geometric organization of its contents.
icml-2026-recursive-binding-on-a-budget-.tldr: Orthogonal Subspace Carving uses geometric projections to encode deep recursive bindings in a fixed-order tensor with constant memory footprint.

paragraphs: Sufficient dimension reduction seeks a small projection of high-dimensional inputs that preserves the response’s conditional mean. Existing gradient-based approaches either struggle with the original dimensionality or incur at least quadratic sample-size costs in each outer iteration. This paper develops a more efficient route to estimating the relevant subspace.

The authors connect minimizers of population MAVE risk to the Grassmannian target approximated by the Outer Product of Gradients method. They reformulate the empirical problem as smooth optimization over the Stiefel manifold, with a closed-form Riemannian gradient. SMAVE combines this formulation with sparse nearest-neighbor localization in projected space and stochastic gradient ascent.

A simplified version has almost-sure convergence and a finite-time rate matching standard nonconvex stochastic first-order scaling. Empirically, SMAVE matches or improves RMAVE’s synthetic subspace recovery at moderate-to-high input dimensions. On four real datasets it improves over OPG and competes with or exceeds RMAVE at orders-of-magnitude lower runtime. The guarantees concern the simplified version, while the broader practical gains come from the reported experiments.
icml-2026-riemannian-stochastic-optimiza.tldr: SMAVE combines geometric stochastic optimization and sparse localization for faster dimension reduction with competitive subspace recovery.

paragraphs: Safety training must improve a language model’s resistance to harmful requests while preserving usefulness. Common adversarial approaches alternate between collecting challenging prompts and training a defender. This paper instead formulates alignment as a non-zero-sum game in which an attacker and defender learn together through online reinforcement learning.

The AdvGame training procedure lets each model adapt continuously to the other’s changing strategies. Rewards come from pairwise preference comparisons rather than separate scores for individual outputs. The authors describe this as more robust supervision that may reduce reward hacking, preserving that benefit as a possibility rather than a guaranteed outcome.

The resulting defender improves both helpfulness and resistance to adversarial attacks, shifting the reported safety–utility trade-off. Training also produces a strong general-purpose attacker that can be applied directly to probe other target models. The contribution therefore concerns both sides of evaluation: jointly adapting policies improve the defended model while yielding a reusable red-teaming agent from the same training process.
icml-2026-safety-alignment-of-lms-via-no.tldr: AdvGame jointly trains attacker and defender language models, improving reported helpfulness and attack resistance while producing a reusable red-teaming agent.

paragraphs: Automatic differentiation makes gradient-based optimization convenient, but some operations provide little useful direction for learning. Thresholds, Boolean decisions, discrete indexing, and sorting can yield zero or undefined gradients. Smooth alternatives exist, yet their implementations are scattered across projects and can be difficult to combine or compare.

SoftJAX and SoftTorch collect these alternatives into libraries designed as replacements for corresponding JAX and PyTorch operations. They cover elementwise functions such as clipping and absolute value, fuzzy-logic utilities for Booleans and indices, and axiswise operations such as sorting and ranking. The latter include approaches based on optimal transport and permutahedron projections.

The libraries also fully support straight-through gradient estimation, expanding the available tools for optimization involving hard operations. Benchmarking and a practical case study demonstrate their use. The contribution is an integrated implementation toolkit: developers can access multiple relaxation techniques through familiar operations instead of assembling disconnected implementations. This makes soft differentiable programming easier to incorporate into workflows that otherwise contain uninformative gradients.
icml-2026-softjax-softtorch-empowering-a.tldr: SoftJAX and SoftTorch provide integrated soft replacements for hard operations that otherwise obstruct gradient-based optimization.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning agents train against objectives and data distributions that change over time. Their internal representations can become unstable or underused as learning proceeds. This paper investigates whether shaping the geometry and distribution of those representations can help agents adapt to changing targets.

The authors establish advantages of isotropic Gaussian embeddings, whose variation is balanced across directions. Under nonstationary targets, these embeddings support stable tracking by linear readouts. They also maximize entropy under a fixed variance budget and encourage balanced use of representational dimensions. The linear-readout setting is an explicit part of the stated tracking result.

Building on these properties, Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization pushes learned representations toward an isotropic Gaussian distribution during training. The method is described as simple and computationally inexpensive. Across multiple domains, experiments show improved performance under nonstationarity and reductions in representation collapse, dormant neurons, and training instability. Together, the theory and experiments motivate representation shaping as a practical way to support more stable adaptation.
icml-2026-stable-deep-reinforcement-lear.tldr: Regularizing representations toward an isotropic Gaussian improves reported reinforcement-learning stability and adaptation to changing targets.

paragraphs: Time-series analysis often requires more than predicting future numbers. Users may need contextual explanations, answers to domain-specific questions, or interpretation alongside unstructured text. Traditional time-series models lack these language capabilities, while language models struggle with inefficient textual representations of numerical sequences and limited numerical pretraining.

TsLLM adds a specialized patch-based encoder-decoder to a language model. It trains on more than 25 billion tokens combining time series and text. Forecasting with context, question answering, anomaly detection, classification, and report generation are all expressed through autoregressive next-token prediction, creating one training framework for diverse numerical and language tasks.

The authors report strong performance where time-series understanding must be integrated with natural language. They explicitly position TsLLM as a general-purpose integration approach rather than a system designed to beat specialized models on traditional benchmarks. Strong zero-shot and few-shot results also show adaptation to new data without additional training. The contribution is a shared interface for numerical perception and language-based interpretation across multiple tasks.
icml-2026-tsllm-augmenting-llms-for-gene.tldr: TsLLM adds specialized time-series perception to a language model for tasks combining numerical signals, context, and natural-language responses.

paragraphs: Natural-language reasoning traces can become lengthy even when they help solve difficult problems. CLSR investigates whether multiple language-model agents can communicate through compact symbolic protocols instead. Each protocol includes symbols, usage rules, and a message-passing contract that can be reused across queries.

Agents invent and refine these protocols through an evolutionary process guided by correctness and token cost. A router selects how to apply them for each query: one inexpensive call, an ensemble of protocols, or several rounds of composition for harder problems. The optimization target is the trade-off between answer accuracy and generated-token expenditure.

Across challenging benchmarks, CLSR reduces generated completion tokens by a factor of three to six relative to standard chain-of-thought while maintaining accuracy. The paper also derives an information-theoretic lower bound on token cost. Its claim that multiround protocols subsume program-execution pipelines is conditional on an interpreter-realizability premise. The empirical and theoretical results therefore address both practical compression and the conditions governing symbolic protocol capabilities.
icml-2026-when-llms-develop-languages-sy.tldr: CLSR evolves and routes compact symbolic communication protocols, reducing reported reasoning-token use three- to sixfold while maintaining accuracy.
